title: Self-serve Fidelity Advisor (SFA) — PRD
author: Leah Summers
body:
Summary
-------
This Product Requirements Document (PRD) describes the Self-serve Fidelity Advisor (SFA): a guided, API-backed recommendation and simulation service that helps Redwood customers choose per-route fidelity configurations (model variant, quantization profile, batching strategy, and caching policy) to meet target latency SLOs and per-token cost budgets while minimizing quality regressions. The SFA is aimed at product engineers, ML engineers, and platform owners operating across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Background and problem statement
--------------------------------
Teams building LLM-powered features must balance latency, cost, and quality. Today, customers either:
- Use default platform recommendations that are conservative (higher cost, higher quality), or
- Manually experiment with model variants, quantization, and batching which is time-consuming and risky for production.
These frictions slow onboarding, increase costs, and lead to avoidable regressions during rollouts. We need a self-serve advisor that reduces trial-and-error, explicitly shows trade-offs, and integrates with our rollout tooling and pricing model.

Scope (what this PRD covers)
---------------------------
1. Recommendation engine that suggests fidelity profiles per API route given: latency SLO, max-per-token budget, and example prompt set.
2. Simulation UI in Console showing expected latency distribution, cost delta, and predicted quality impact (delta from baseline) with visual trade-off sliders.
3. API endpoints to run offline scans: submit a small prompt corpus + SLO + budget -> returns candidate profiles ranked by trade-off score.
4. Integration hooks for: rollouts (canary/A-B), Optimize suggestions, and per-route billing preview.

Out of scope
------------
- Automatic rollout enforcement (SFA will recommend and produce rollout configs; a separate rollout service will execute).
- Low-level runtime kernel changes; SFA will emit profiles compatible with existing runtime execution paths.
- On-prem air-gapped installers in first release (beta will support VPC deployments with telemetry).

Goals and success metrics
-------------------------
Primary goals:
- Reduce time-to-production fidelity tuning from days to hours for 80% of experimental customers.
- Enable 20% average per-token cost savings for customers who adopt recommendations without exceeding quality regression tolerance.

Success metrics (measurable):
- Adoption: % of new Dedicated customers who use SFA within first 30 days (target 40% in Q1 post-launch).
- Accuracy: Fraction of SFA-chosen profiles that achieve target latency SLO in production within a 10% margin (target 85%).
- Cost impact: Average per-token cost delta for adopters relative to baseline profile (target -15% pct).
- Quality/regression: % of adopters with automated eval degradation alerts > threshold (target < 10%).

User personas
------------
- ML Engineer (MLOps): cares about throughput, quantization, and model fidelity. Wants a reproducible recommendation API and config outputs for CI.
- Product Engineer: focused on latency and end-user quality. Wants quick UI feedback and safe canary rollout recipe.
- Platform Admin (Enterprise): wants cost transparency and per-tenant guardrails; requires restricted recommendations and audit logs.

User journeys
------------
1. Console quick path: Product Engineer selects a route, sets latency SLO and budget, uploads 50 example prompts -> sees recommended profiles, compares simulated token cost & histogram, clicks "apply to canary" to create rollout config.
2. API batch path: MLOps submits a corpus and desired targets via SFA API -> receives JSON candidates -> stores selected profile in CI for scheduled rollout.
3. Enterprise review path: Platform Admin requests advisor output for tenant X, reviews audit trail and toggles restricted recommendations (disallow quantization beyond Q2).

Functional requirements (priority 1..3)
--------------------------------------
- FR-1 (P1): Recommendation API: POST /sfa/v1/recommend with payload: route_id, example_prompts (<=500 tokens each, max 200), latency_slo_ms, cost_budget_usd_per_1M_tokens -> returns ranked profiles with estimated p50/p95 latency, per-token cost, predicted quality_delta.
- FR-2 (P1): Console Simulation view: interactive chart with sliders for SLO and budget and a table of candidate profiles (model, quant, batching, cache settings), exportable JSON rollout recipe.
- FR-3 (P1): Profile schema: fidelity_profile variant (string), quant_profile (string), batch_policy_id (string), cache_policy_id (string), expected_cpu/gpu_units (numeric estimate), estimated_cost_per_1k_tokens (USD), predicted_quality_delta_pct (float).
- FR-4 (P2): Guardrails: per-tenant constraints enforced by policy engine; advisors honor tenant-level max-quantization and approved variants.
- FR-5 (P2): Simulation accuracy lab: with ground-truth microbench suite, SFA must store test results and produce a confidence score for each profile.
- FR-6 (P2): Telemetry output: advisor decisions and input corpus hashed (PII removed) emitted to telemetry with tags: route_id, tenant_id, model_family, profile_id, decision_confidence, timestamp.
- FR-7 (P3): Cost-preview in billing system: SFA results should surface a billed delta estimate in Console for customer review before applying.

Non-functional requirements
---------------------------
- NFR-1: Recommendation latency: synchronous API calls must return within 5s for sample corpuses <= 20 prompts; larger scans can be async.
- NFR-2: Throughput: service must support 200 concurrent small recommendations (P95) in GA.
- NFR-3: Security: inputs may include customer prompts (sensitive). For Hosted and Dedicated, data retention limited to 30 days for SFA artifacts; for Private, default retention is 0 days unless customer opts-in. All stored corpora must be hashed and access-controlled.
- NFR-4: Privacy: PII scrubbing pipeline applied before any storage or model-based simulation.
- NFR-5: Explainability: UI must display top 3 factors driving a recommendation (e.g., "KV cache hit ratio expected to be 72%", "quantization introduces estimated -2.6% BLEU on eval set").

Quality & evaluation plan
-------------------------
- Prelaunch benchmark matrix: run SFA candidate profiles across standard workloads (conversational, retrieval-augmented, summarization) and measure model output quality vs. baseline using existing eval harness.
- Continuous monitoring: define a per-profile regression alert based on eval loss increase or task-specific metric drop > configurable threshold.

API contract (example)
----------------------
Request (POST /sfa/v1/recommend):
{\n  "route_id": "customer-123/chat/messages",\n  "latency_slo_ms": 120,\n  "cost_budget_usd_per_1M_tokens": 150.00,\n  "example_prompts": ["Summarize latest order status for the user.", "Generate 3 possible follow-up questions for support agent."]\n}

Response (200):
{\n  "candidates": [\n    {"profile_id": "p-optim-02", "variant":"rw-8k-opt","quant_profile":"int8-2","p50_ms":"68","p95_ms":"110","est_cost_per_1k":"0.012","pred_quality_delta_pct":"-0.8","confidence":"0.92"},\n    {"profile_id": "p-safe-01", "variant":"rw-16k","quant_profile":"fp16","p50_ms":"95","p95_ms":"140","est_cost_per_1k":"0.022","pred_quality_delta_pct":"0.0","confidence":"0.96"}\n  ]\n}

(Above JSON is illustrative; real API will return numeric values not strings.)

Console UX and visualizations
-----------------------------
Key screens:
1. Route Recommendation Landing: form to set SLO, budget, and select prompt corpus (upload or use captured samples).
2. Simulation results: side-by-side candidate cards, cost delta, latency histograms, and an "impact explanation" section.
3. Rollout builder: convert a selected profile into a canary rollout that ties to our existing rollout APIs with automatic fallback thresholds.

Telemetry and data requirements
-------------------------------
Required telemetry keys (examples):
- sfa.request.id (UUID)
- tenant.id
- route.id
- profile.id
- p50_ms_estimate, p95_ms_estimate
- est_cost_per_1k_tokens
- predicted_quality_delta_pct
- decision_confidence
- seed_eval_metrics (hashed id referencing stored eval result)
Retention & access: telemetry raw payloads retained 90 days for diagnostics; sanitized decision metadata retained 18 months for product analytics.

Roadmap and milestones (high level)
-----------------------------------
- Alpha (Q1 2028, internal): Console prototype + synchronous API for small corpora, limited to Hosted. Focus: core recommendations and basic UI.
- Beta (Q2 2028): Add Dedicated and VPC support, async scan mode, confidence scoring, and guardrails. Invite pilot customers.
- GA (Q4 2028): Full rollout with billing preview, platform-wide rollout integration, and enterprise audit controls.

Pricing and packaging implications
--------------------------------
- SFA will be offered as: free-tier recommendations for small scans (<=20 prompts) for all customers; credit-based scans for larger workloads (per-scan compute credit consumption) and an Enterprise SFA add-on that includes extended retention, audit exports, and private-preview modelling compute.
- Billing preview: when applying a profile, Console shows estimated monthly delta by projected usage tiers. This requires integration with usage analytics to map per-route traffic.

Rollout plan and migration guidance
----------------------------------
1. Internal alpha: product + runtime engineers validate simulation vs. bench results.
2. Pilot customers: invite 6 customers (mix of startups and mid-market) to test integrations and provide corpora.
3. Staged beta: opt-in in Console for Dedicated customers; collect telemetry and iterate.
4. GA: enable self-serve for Hosted and opt-in for Private (with on-prem telemetry hooks).
Migration guidance for customers: preserve existing profiles as baselines; SFA produces a clear JSON recipe and confidence score. Recommend 1-week canary (5% traffic) followed by 24–72 hour observability window before ramp.

Launch checklist
----------------
- [ ] Instrument telemetry and events (keys above).
- [ ] Console wireframes implemented and usability-tested.
- [ ] API contract finalized and published.
- [ ] Guardrails/policy controls implemented.
- [ ] Pilot customers onboarded and signed beta agreements.
- [ ] Pricing model approved by finance.

Owners and stakeholders
-----------------------
- Product owner: Leah Summers (Roadmap, prioritization)
- Engineering lead: Darren Wu (Recommendation engine, API)
- UX: Marta Lopez (Console flows)
- Applied ML: Ravi Kapoor (quality prediction and eval harness)
- SRE: Priya Nanda (capacity & availability)
- Finance & Pricing: Elena Markov (packaging and billing integration)

Open questions and risks
-----------------------
- Prediction accuracy risk: model quality delta predictions may under/over-estimate change; mitigated by confidence scores and forced canary defaults.
- Privacy/regulatory risk: customer corpus may contain PII; require robust scrubbing and tenant opt-in for retention.
- Cost of analytics: large-scale simulations could be expensive; initial pricing must reflect compute costs.

Appendix A: Example fidelity_profile table
-----------------------------------------
| field | example | notes |
|---|---|---|
| profile_id | p-optim-02 | stable id used in rollouts |
| variant | rw-8k-opt | model family / variant |
| quant_profile | int8-2 | quantization spec name |
| batch_policy_id | bp-small-latency | reference to batch policy table |
| cache_policy_id | cache-prefix-high | recommended KV/prefix cache policy |
| est_cost_per_1k | $0.012 | estimated cost per 1k tokens |
| predicted_quality_delta_pct | -0.8 | negative implies slight degradation |

Appendix B: Related pages and dependencies
------------------------------------------
- tenant-fidelity-experiments-and-guardrails-prd-2025-03-11 (experimental guardrails)
- fidelity-packages-and-customer-migration-playbook-2028-01-24 (migration guidance)
- optimize-1-3-release-notes-performance-profiles-2026-02-18 (references to performance profiles used in simulation)

Document maintenance
--------------------
Owner (Product) will review this PRD quarterly and after each major pilot phase. Changes must be recorded in the page history and communicated to the stakeholders list.
